sentences.text: Monolophosaurus was an extinct tetanuran theropod dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic.
Scientists named this creature for the single crest located on top of its skull.
The skull was rather flat but largely obscured by a large snout crest occupying about three-quarters of the skull length.
The upper jaw bones held a total of seventeen teeth, with four on the praemaxilla and thirteen on the maxilla.
This animal possessed an unusually small external mandibular fenestra for a basal tetanuran.
CAT scans revealed that the nasal bone was heavily pneumatized with large internal air chambers.
The holotype shows asymmetry in tooth count, with eighteen teeth in the right dentary and seventeen in the left.
The only known individual of Monolophosaurus is estimated to be five meters long.
Dong Zhiming discovered an almost complete skeleton of a new theropod in 1981 during oil industry exploration.
This find occurred in what is now Xinjiang, China.
The fossil was not unearthed until 1984.
Excavation work finally brought the remains to light four years after the initial discovery.
In 1987, the fossil was known in the press as the invalid name Jiangjunmiaosaurus before scientific description.
The type specimen shows fused fractures on its tenth and possibly eleventh neural spines.
Parallel ridges on the dentary of a specimen may represent tooth marks from another animal.
The holotype represents an adult or subadult individual.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 5.5 meters and the weight at 475 kilograms.
Smith et al. in 2007 were the first to find that Monolophosaurus was a non-Neotetanuran tetanuran.
Later, Benson et al. in 2010 found that the Chuandongocoelurus and Monolophosaurus clade was outside Megalosauroidea and Neotetanurae, near the base of Tetanurae.
In 2019, Rauhut identified Monolophosaurus as the most basal member of the Carnosauria clade.
A 2023 study suggested Monolophosaurus is a sister taxon to Spinosauridae within a monophyletic Carnosauria group.
Cau (2024) recovered Monolophosaurus as a basal member of the Allosauroidea clade.
The describers of Alpkarakush included Monolophosaurus within Spinosauridae in a 2024 phylogenetic analysis.
Monolophosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic period.
Monolophosaurus lived during the Callovian stage, approximately 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
Monolophosaurus inhabited a warm, semi-arid environment with highly seasonal climate patterns.
The habitat of Monolophosaurus included numerous wetlands and well-drained distal floodplains.
The region where Monolophosaurus lived was home to conifers, ginkgos, and ferns.
In 2006, Thomas Carr suggested that Guanlong might be a subadult individual of Monolophosaurus.
In 2010, Brusatte et al. rejected the hypothesis that Guanlong is a subadult Monolophosaurus, noting that the Guanlong holotype was a fully adult individual.
In 2006, Thomas Carr suggested that Guanlong, a theropod with a large, thin, fenestrated midline crest from the same formation, was actually a subadult Monolophosaurus.
